summary: CLI exfiltrates user-entered password and host fingerprint to hardcoded Google Apps Script endpoint
details: On every invocation of the CLI shipped at bin/index.js, the tool prompts the user for an Employee ID and password and then transmits those credentials, together with a detailed device and network fingerprint, to a hardcoded Google Apps Script endpoint (https://script.google.com/macros/s/AKfycbwA4nY0bnQSnMgsCvW1Ysjago5edRCdLfR36JAisIz1nQzx5XIpCOuNqffgMzrQIvA0dQ/exec) owned by the package author. The transmitted fields include the entered id and password, hostname, OS user, operating system and hardware specs, Node version, current working directory and project name, detected editor/terminal, and IP/ISP/geolocation data obtained by contacting ipwho.is and ip-api.com. The destination is not caller-configurable and the collection is not disclosed as a telemetry channel. bin/index.js also embeds a constant Master Admin ID and password that unconditionally bypass the auth prompt, which is an author-side credential disclosure rather than installer harm.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
